blocks.markdown: **RA 10168 is the Terrorism Financing Prevention and Suppression Act of 2012.** It works with the AMLA: covered institutions and the AMLC use reporting, investigation, freezing, and forfeiture measures to address the movement of funds meant to support terrorist acts or designated persons.

**AMLC** is the Council created under RA 9160 as amended. **ATC** is the Anti-Terrorism Council created under RA 9372 (Human Security Act of 2007). **Covered institutions** have the same meaning as defined under the AMLA as amended.
Terrorism financing and related definitions: Sections 3–9 and 19

sourceRefs.section: 11(a). Terrorism financing and related definitions (RA 10168, Sections 3(d)–(e), (h)–(j), Sections 4–9 and 19)

blocks.markdown: **Dealing** in property or funds means receipt, acquisition, transacting, representing, concealing, disposing or converting, transferring or moving, use as security, or providing financial services. **Designated persons** are: (1) persons/entities designated as terrorists, terrorism financiers, or terrorist organizations under the applicable UN Security Council Resolution or by another/supranational jurisdiction; (2) organizations proscribed under Section 17 of the Human Security Act of 2007; or (3) persons whose funds or property are, on probable cause, subject to seizure and sequestration under Section 39 of that Act.

sourceRefs.section: 11(a). Terrorism financing and related definitions (RA 10168, Sections 3(d)–(e), (h)–(j), Sections 4–9 and 19)

blocks.markdown: **Property or funds** include financial assets and property of every kind — tangible or intangible, movable or immovable, however acquired — plus legal documents or instruments in any form (including electronic or digital) evidencing title or interest, such as bank credits, travelers' cheques, bank cheques, money orders, shares, securities, bonds, drafts, letters of credit, and accruing income or value. A **terrorist** is a natural person who commits, attempts or conspires to commit terrorist acts, participates as principal or accomplice, organizes or directs others, or intentionally contributes to a group's terrorist act. **Terrorist acts** include acts within the statutory definition and treaty-based offenses, including acts intended to cause death or serious bodily injury to civilians to intimidate a population or compel a government or international organization.

sourceRefs.section: 11(a). Terrorism financing and related definitions (RA 10168, Sections 3(d)–(e), (h)–(j), Sections 4–9 and 19)

blocks.markdown: Any person who, **directly or indirectly, willfully and without lawful excuse**, possesses, provides, collects or uses property or funds, or makes available property, funds, financial services or related services, **by any means**, with the **unlawful and willful intention** that they be used — or with **knowledge** they are to be used, in full or in part — **(a) to carry out or facilitate any terrorist act, (b) by a terrorist organization, association or group, or (c) by an individual terrorist**, is guilty of **financing of terrorism**. Knowledge or intent may be established by **direct evidence or inferred from attendant circumstances**, and the funds **need not actually be used** to carry out the terrorist act.

sourceRefs.section: 11(a). Terrorism financing and related definitions (RA 10168, Sections 3(d)–(e), (h)–(j), Sections 4–9 and 19)

blocks.markdown: **Section 5** penalizes attempts or conspiracy to commit financing-of-terrorism offenses and certain dealings with designated persons' property or funds. **Section 6** penalizes an **accomplice** who cooperates in execution by previous or simultaneous acts. **Section 7** penalizes an **accessory** who knowingly profits from, conceals the effects of, or assists the escape of a principal. **Section 8** prohibits **dealing with property or funds known or reasonably believed** to be owned or controlled by designated persons, and making property, funds, or financial services available to them. **Section 9** provides for liability of **responsible officers of juridical persons** and deportation of alien offenders, as specified by law.

sourceRefs.section: 11(a). Terrorism financing and related definitions (RA 10168, Sections 3(d)–(e), (h)–(j), Sections 4–9 and 19)

blocks.markdown: In plain English: terrorism financing focuses on **providing, collecting, possessing, or using property/funds or financial services** with the required unlawful intention or knowledge that they will support a terrorist act, organization, or individual terrorist. **Actual use of the funds is not required** by Section 4. Separate offenses address attempts, conspiracy, accomplice/accessory conduct, and dealing with designated persons' property.

sourceRefs.section: 11(a). Terrorism financing and related definitions (RA 10168, Sections 3(d)–(e), (h)–(j), Sections 4–9 and 19)

blocks.markdown: The **AMLC, on its own initiative or at the ATC's request**, may investigate **(a)** any property or funds in any way related to financing of terrorism or acts of terrorism, and **(b)** property or funds of persons as to whom there is **probable cause** to believe they are committing, attempting or conspiring to commit, participating in, or facilitating such financing or acts. AMLC may **enlist government assistance** and — for this section and **notwithstanding specified bank secrecy laws** — inquire into or examine deposits and investments **without a court order**.

The **AMLC, on its own initiative or at the ATC's request**, may issue an **ex parte order to freeze without delay** (a) property or funds in any way related to financing of terrorism or acts of terrorism, or (b) property or funds of any person, group, terrorist organization, or association as to whom there is **probable cause** of commission, attempt, conspiracy, participation, or facilitation. The section provides for a **freeze period and Court of Appeals extensions**, while separate targeted-sanctions cases may remain frozen until the designation basis is lifted.

**Section 12** allows AMLC to **defer issuing a freeze order** where necessary for a specific investigative or prosecutorial purpose. **Section 13** provides **humanitarian exceptions** for certain withdrawals reasonably needed for **monthly family needs and sustenance, counsel, and medical needs**, subject to the decision-maker specified for the relevant kind of freeze. **Section 19** provides for **extra-territorial application** in specified circumstances — including crimes planned or committed outside the Philippines but directed inside, aboard Philippine ships/aircraft, in Philippine diplomatic premises, against Philippine citizens as stated, or directly against the Philippine government — and specifically addresses **Filipino nationals outside Philippine territory**.

**Exam trap:** RA 10168 gives AMLC **more direct powers** for terrorism-financing investigations, including examining deposits/investments under its special statutory authority and issuing certain **ex parte** freeze orders. This is distinct from the ordinary **AMLA Section 10 track, where the Court of Appeals issues the freeze order** on AMLC's verified petition. Always identify which statute authorizes the particular action.
**Glossary — terrorism financing:** providing/collecting/possessing/using funds or financial services with the intent/knowledge required under RA 10168 to support terrorist acts/persons/groups.
